story.title: Document management was the first thing SaaS came for and the thing SaaS got wrong.
body: The last decade's answer was a subscription portal, a monthly bill, and the expectation that your clients' files would live on hardware you had never seen. For a sole-trader electrician or a three-partner law firm, that was never a good trade.

The mistake was treating document management as a cloud problem. It is a filing problem. A tradie needs job folders they can find next Tuesday; a solicitor needs matter files with an audit trail that holds up at a Law Society review. Neither needs their documents to leave the office.

Adapdev started from the other end. One development team, one product line (ADMS), and a stubborn preference for software that installs on hardware you own, speaks the client/matter/job language you already use, and keeps running when the internet is down.
That is the whole idea. Everything in ADMS exists to make it the easiest way to file a document in Australia, and the hardest way to accidentally lose one.

rules.title: A few things we will not do

items.text: No cloud lock-in. Your database is on your hardware. If you stop paying Adapdev, ADMS keeps running and your files stay yours.

texture.alt: Folded fabric lit from the side

items.text: No per-document pricing. One licence per installation. File ten documents or ten million — the price is the same.
No tier-one support queue. The developer who shipped the release is the person who answers the bug report.
No account you didn't create. There is no sign-up screen, no mandatory telemetry, no email list you got added to.
